newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha higher, contango shrinks further.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha higher, contango shrinks further.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices rose in afternoon trade on Tuesday, pushed up by strong gains in crude futures, traders said.

Contango in near-term naphtha cargoes continued to shrink amid firming sentiment for prompt cargoes. The one-month spread from the first of half July was discussed at minus 50 cents/even. It was traded at minus 60 cents on Monday.
Strength in near-term cargoes was mainly attributed by traders to the closure of the East-West arbitrage window.
Bids for second-half July open-spec naphtha were heard at $211.50 per tonne against offers at $212.00.
It was assessed at $209.00/209.50 in late Monday trading.
First-half July was quoted at $211.00/212.00, compared with Monday's $208.00/209.00.

In naphtha term talks in Singapore, Saudi Aramco was rumoured to be targetting a $17.00 to $17.50 premium for A-180 to be lifted at Ras Tanura on the Gulf coast. The current price is $6.50 per tonne over the Aramco formula

Thirteen potential buyers of Aramco naphtha, including nine Japanese firms, are in Singapore this week for term-price talks on Aramco naphtha cargoes to be loaded in the second half of 1997. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
